rounds.text: Manraj Housing Finance is demonstrating a powerful earnings turnaround, characterized by a 63% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E12] and a net profit increase of 88% year-over-year [E30]. This growth significantly outpaces the sector median profit growth of 24.9% [E35], while the company delivers a superior Return on Equity (ROE) of 22.75% compared to the sector benchmark of 4.91% [E8]. Despite this accelerating earnings profile [E32], the market has yet to recognize the shift, as recent profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by a substantial 105% [E26]. The stock currently sits at just 9% of its 52-week range [E4], suggesting that the market is pricing the company based on stale sentiment rather than its improving financial results [E33]. Conceded: the company faces significant headwinds including a negative book value [E1], negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.53 Cr [E18], and a low interest coverage ratio [E28]. Nevertheless, the three-year compounded share price growth of 20% suggests a baseline of long-term value that the current market price, down 42% over the last year, may be overlooking [E13, E14].

Manraj Housing Finance Ltd carries severe fundamental risks that are obscured by superficial profit metrics, led by a deeply compromised balance sheet featuring a negative book value of ₹ -1.58 [E1]. This negative equity results in distorted and negative valuation multiples, including a price-to-book ratio of -21.52x and a negative P/E of -94.44x [E1, E5]. Operational efficiency is severely lacking, evidenced by a negative return on capital employed of -2.4% and a negative return on assets of -0.87% against a sector benchmark of 1.92% [E7, E11]. Furthermore, cash generation is non-existent, with operating and free cash flows both resting at a negative Rs -0.53 Cr for March 2026, while total borrowings increased to Rs 20.05 Cr [E18, E19, E20]. Institutional desertion compounds these risks, as domestic institutions have completely exited their holdings, dropping from 7.19% in September 2023 to 0.00% by June 2026 alongside flagged concerns regarding a low interest coverage ratio [E23, E28]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing profit growth of 63% and a 22.75% ROE that outperforms the sector benchmark [E8, E12].

Conceded: the balance sheet shows a negative book value of ₹ -1.58 resulting in distorted multiples [E1]. However, dismissing the business on these metrics ignores explosive operational momentum, led by compounded profit growth of 63% and a net profit surge of 88% year-over-year [E12, E30]. The bear highlights negative cash flow [E18, E19], but the business prints a strong 22.75% ROE that easily beats the sector benchmark of 4.91% [E8]. While institutional holdings dropped to 0.00% [E23], insider alignment remains rock-solid with promoters holding 62.83% steadily since September 2023 [E22]. The insider-bias checklist explicitly warns not to dismiss a turnaround on stale sentiment, noting that results are actively improving with a score of 76 out of 100 while profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 105% [E26, E33].

Conceded: compounded profit growth stands at 63% and net profit grew 88% year-over-year [E12, E30]. However, this operational momentum is completely undermined by negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.53 Cr as of March 2026, rendering cash conversion entirely distressed [E17, E18, E19]. Conceded: the reported ROE is 22.75% [E8]. That figure, however, is a statistical artifact of a fundamentally impaired balance sheet carrying a negative book value of ₹ -1.58 and negative net worth, which also explains the deeply distorted price-to-book and negative ROCE figures [E1, E9, E11]. The bull's reliance on stable promoter ownership ignores the stark reality that domestic institutions have entirely abandoned the stock, liquidating their holdings from 7.19% down to 0.00% [E22, E23]. Finally, pointing to a turnaround score ignores the company's explicit negative flag for a low interest coverage ratio alongside rising borrowings of Rs 20.05 Cr [E20, E28].
